AccessEvent.doc:
A change assistive technology should hear about (`App.on_access`):
`kind` is "focus" (keyboard focus moved to `node`), "value" (the focused
widget's name, value or states changed) or "announce" (`App.announce`:
`node.name` is the message).

AccessNode.doc:
One thing in the accessibility tree (`App.accessibility()`) — what a
screen reader is told about a widget or one of its items: `role`
("button", "checkbox", "textbox", "list", "listitem", "tab", "menuitem",
...), `name` (what it's called), `value` (a field's text, a slider's
number, the selected option), `description`, `states` ("focused",
"disabled", "checked", "selected", "expanded"...), its box, `children`,
and the `widget` it came from (null for items). `level` is the depth of
a tree item.

Animation.doc:
A running animation (`app.animate`). `cancel()` stops it (no more
`on_step`, no `on_done`); `done` says whether it has finished.

App.doc:
A web app: routes, middleware, error handling, and a server.

    app := web.App()
    app.get("/", fn(req, res) { res.text("hi") })
    app.listen(3000)

Routes run in the order added; the first whose method and path match
answers. `views` is the templates folder for `res.render`.

Bool.doc: Boolean type. Only two values: `true` and `false`.

Button.doc:
A button. `on_click()` runs when it's clicked — pass `on_click=fn() {...}`,
or subclass Button and override `on_click(self)`.

A push button. `on_click` (no arguments) runs when it's clicked, or
when it has the focus and Enter / Space is pressed.

Callable.doc:
A first-class function value produced by a lambda expression (`fn(...) => ...`).
Callables can be stored in variables, passed as arguments, and invoked
by higher-order methods such as `List.map`, `List.filter`, and `List.each`.

@example:
double := fn(x: Int) => x * 2
print(double(21))                      // 42
evens := [1, 2, 3, 4].filter(fn(x: Int) => x % 2 == 0)

Canvas.doc:
A widget you draw yourself: `on_draw(win, x, y, width, height)` runs every
frame (drawing is clipped to the canvas), `on_event(e)` gets its mouse
events (coordinates are the window's) and keys while it has the focus.
`width` / `height` are the size it asks for; with `expand` it takes free
space.

Checkbox.doc: A box that's ticked or not, with a label; `on_change(checked)` when it's clicked.

A box that's ticked or not, with a label. `on_change(checked)` runs when
the user toggles it.

ColorPicker.doc:
Pick a colour: a square for saturation (left → right) and brightness
(bottom → top), a strip for the hue, and a swatch with its hex code.
Drag in either, or with the focus: Left / Right saturation, Up / Down
brightness, Page Up / Page Down hue. `color` is the colour (a `window`
colour Int); `on_change(color)` runs when it changes.

Column.doc: Widgets one above the other, `spacing` pixels apart.

Children stacked top to bottom, each as wide as the column. Free height
goes to children with `expand = true`.

Component.doc:
A component: a struct with its state in fields and its HTML in a template — returned from `template()` (a raw string, `r"""..."""`), or in the file named after the struct (`counter_page.html`) next to the `.qk` file:

Count: {{ count }}

calls self.add(1) self.draft follows the field; Enter calls self.save(text)
calls self.close() 3 s after it appears another component, by its struct's name {% if count >= 10 %}

a lot

{% end %} {% for i, item in items %}
  • {{ item }}
    • {% else %}
  • none
    • {% end %} CSS for this component's elements only `on_load()` sets it up (once). Events call its methods by name; the page is rendered again after each one. Props: `text="hi {{ name }}"` sets the child's `text` field (a String), `:count="n + 1"` sets it to the value; `@done="refresh"` runs when the child calls `self.emit("done")`. A `` in a component's template shows what its tag enclosed. A page is a Component served by a `live.Router` (usually a `live.Page`). `title()` sets the page title; `self.go(path)` sends the browser to another page. (The 1.0 way, overriding `render()` and `handle(event, data)` with `q-click="name"` attributes, still works.)

Database.doc:
A connection to a database (`sqlite.open`). Each method runs one statement
and is done with it: nothing to finalize or reset.

Parameters: `?` in the SQL with a List (in order), or `:name` with a Map:
    db.query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE a = ? AND b = ?", [1, "x"])
    db.query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE a = :a AND b = :b", {"a": 1, "b": "x"})
Values go in as they are — never pasted into the SQL, so they can't change
it. Int, Double, String, Bool (stored as 1 / 0) and null.

Rows come back as Maps, column name → value: Int, Double, String or null
(SQLite has no Bool: a stored `true` reads back as 1).

DatePicker.doc:
A date field that opens a month calendar. `year`, `month` (1-12), `day`;
`text()` is "YYYY-MM-DD". Click the field (or Space / Enter / Alt+Down) to
open it; in the calendar click a day, `<` / `>` change month, arrows move
by day / week, Page Up / Page Down by month, Enter picks, Escape closes.
`on_change(year, month, day)` runs when the date changes.

DateTime.doc:
Snapshot of a moment in time. Construct via `datetime.now()`,
`datetime.from_unix(s)`, or `datetime.from_iso(s)` rather than calling
`__init` directly.

Double.doc:
64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point number.

@example:
x := 3.14
print(x.ceil())    // 4.0
print(x.str())     // "3.14"

Dropdown.doc:
A list to pick one of `options` from; `selected` is the index shown.
`on_change(index, option)` when another is picked.

Pick one of `options` (anything with `.str()`) from a list that opens
below the field. Click it, or Space / Enter / Alt+Down when focused;
Up / Down change the choice directly while it's closed. `selected` is
the index; `on_change(index, item)` runs when it changes.

Event.doc:
Something that happened to a window. `kind` is one of:
  "close"       — the close button (or Ctrl+C / quit); the window closes
                  unless `keep_open` was set
  "key_down" / "key_up" — `key` is the key's name in lower case: "a",
                  "escape", "return", "space", "left", "f1", "left_shift"...;
                  `repeat` is true for auto-repeat; `shift` / `ctrl` /
                  `alt` / `meta` say which modifiers were held
  "text"        — typed text (`text`), with the keyboard layout and
                  accents applied — use this for text entry, not key_down
  "compose"     — an input method (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, dead keys...)
                  is composing `text`: show it at the cursor (underlined)
                  until it arrives as a "text" event; `cursor` is the
                  position inside it and `length` how much of it the
                  input method has selected (characters). An empty
                  `text` ends the composition. See `text_input_area`.
  "access"      — a screen reader asks for `action` ("invoke", "toggle",
                  "set_value", "set_range", "select", "expand",
                  "collapse", "focus") on node `target` of the tree sent
                  with `access_update`; `text` is the new value. `ui`
                  handles these itself.
  "mouse_move"  — `x`, `y`; `left` true while the left button is held
  "mouse_down" / "mouse_up" — `x`, `y`, `button` (1 left, 2 middle,
                  3 right), `clicks` (2 for a double click)
  "wheel"       — `dx`, `dy` (positive = away from you / right)
  "resize"      — new `width`, `height`
  "focus" / "blur" — the window gained / lost keyboard focus

EventStream.doc:
An open Server-Sent Events stream (Response.event_stream()). In a
TestClient, what's sent is kept in `sent`: a List of [event, data].

FieldError.doc:
``: the error of the component's field `email`, in a `

` (hidden when there's none; a screen reader says it when it appears).

File.doc:
A handle for reading and writing to the OS file system.
Supports the `with` statement for automatic close on scope exit.

Use `sys.stdin()`, `sys.stdout()`, `sys.stderr()` to wrap the standard
streams as Files (those wrappers ignore `close()`).

FileDialog.doc:
A window-sized dialog to pick a file (`mode="open"`), a name to save as
(`mode="save"`) or a folder (`mode="folder"`), starting in `dir`.
`filter` (e.g. "*.qk") limits the files shown. `show()` opens it;
`on_pick(path)` runs with the full path chosen, `on_cancel()` (optional)
when it's dismissed. Double-click or Enter opens a folder or picks a
file; Backspace goes up a folder; Tab moves between the list and the
name field; Escape cancels. While it's open it takes all input.

FileIterator.doc:
Iterator over a file's lines. Produced by `for line in file { ... }`.
Each `__next` call reads one line via `File.read_line`.

Font.doc:
A TrueType / OpenType font at one pixel size (`window.load_font`). Pass
it to `Window.text(..., font=f)`. Text is UTF-8 — any character the font
has is drawn. `size` is the requested height; `ascent` / `descent` are
how far glyphs reach above / below the baseline, `line_height` the
distance between lines. One Font works in every window.

Html.doc:
HTML of your own, as is (not escaped — don't put user input in it
unescaped; `live.html(template, data)` escapes for you).

HttpError.doc:
Throw from a handler to answer with `status` and `message` — e.g.
`throw web.HttpError(404, "no such user")`. The app's error handler gets
it (the default one sends the status and message).

Image.doc: A picture; `alt` describes it (for screen readers).
An image loaded for one window (`Window.load_image`); `width` / `height` in pixels.

Int.doc:
64-bit signed integer.
Supports arithmetic operators (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`; `n.pow(e)` for powers) and comparisons.

@example:
n := 42
print(n.str())       // "42"
print(n.is_even())   // true
print(n.pow(2))      // 1764

KvResult.doc:
Key + value extracted from a `key = value` line. Bare-key syntax only
for now (no quoted keys).

Label.doc:
Text. "\n" starts a new line. `color` -1 uses the theme's text colour;
`align` is "left", "center" or "right".

Link.doc:
A link to another page. Between live pages it switches without a reload
(Back / Forward work); `external=true` for a normal link (another site).

List.signature: struct List : Printable, Representable, Sizeable, Iterable {
List.doc:
A dynamic, ordered sequence of values of any type.
Elements are zero-indexed. Lists grow automatically as items are appended.

@example:
nums := [1, 2, 3]
nums.append(4)
print(nums.length())    // 4
print(nums[0])          // 1
doubled := nums.map(fn(x: Int) => x * 2)

ListItem.doc:
An entry for a ListView or a Table cell with an `icon` (an image file,
drawn at the text's height) before its `text`; `data` keeps anything you
want with it. Its `.str()` is `text`, so sorting and `on_select` work as
with plain strings.

ListView.doc:
A bulleted list of `items` — text, or widgets. With `on_select`, an item
can be clicked: `on_select(index, item)`.

A scrollable list of items (anything with `.str()`), one selectable.
`on_select(index, item)` runs when the selection changes; `selected` is
the index (-1 = none). `rows` sets how many rows it asks room for.

Map.doc:
A hash map (dictionary) that associates `String` keys with values of any type.
Insertion order is not guaranteed. All keys must be `String`.

@example:
m := {}
m.put("name", "Alice")
m.put("age", 30)
print(m.get("name"))    // "Alice"
print(m.has("age"))     // true
m.remove("age")
print(m.length())       // 1

Match.doc:
Result of `Regex.find`. `start` and `end` are character positions in the input
String; `text` is the substring `[start, end)`; `groups` is a `List<String>`
of the captured groups (group 0 = full match is NOT included — `text` is
the whole match).

MemoryStore.doc: Sessions in the server's memory (the default).

Menu.doc:
A list of `ui.MenuItem`s that pops up: under a `ui.MenuBar` title, or
where the user right-clicks a widget whose `context_menu` it is
(`menu.open_at(x, y)` from code). Click an item, or Up / Down and Enter;
Escape closes it.

MenuBar.doc:
A row of menu titles, usually at the top of the window:
`ui.MenuBar(["File", "Edit"], [file_menu, edit_menu])`. Click a title to
open its menu; while one is open, moving over another title (or Left /
Right) switches to it.

MenuItem.doc:
One entry of a `ui.Menu`: `text`, `on_click` (no arguments), an optional
`shortcut` label shown on the right (just text — bind the keys yourself
with `app.on_key`), and `enabled`. `ui.MenuItem("-")` is a separator.

Palette.doc:
A command palette / quick open: a search field over a list, at the top of
the window (under the title bar). `on_query(text) -> List` gives the rows
for what's typed — `PaletteItem`s, or anything with `.str()`; Enter or a
click runs `on_pick(item)`, Escape or a click outside closes it
(`on_cancel()`). Up / Down (wrapping), Page Up / Page Down, Home / End
(with Ctrl) move. `show(text)` opens it with `text` typed.

    p := ui.Palette(on_query=fn(q) { return rows_for(q) }, on_pick=fn(it) { run(it) },
                    placeholder="Type a command")
    p.show()        // e.g. from Ctrl+Shift+P

PaletteItem.doc:
A row of a `Palette`: its `label`, a muted `detail` after it (a file's
folder), a `hint` on the right (a shortcut), any `data`. `marks` /
`detail_marks` are character indices drawn in the accent colour — the
letters a fuzzy match found.

Panel.signature: define Panel(children: List, padding: Int = 12, spacing: Int = 8, expand: Bool = false) -> Column {
Panel.doc: A Column drawn on a raised surface with a border (12px padding by default).

Parseable.doc:
Implemented by types that can be constructed from a string representation.
Pairs naturally with `Printable` — a round-trip of `parse(val.str())` should
return the original value.

@example
n := Int.parse("42")     // 42
d := Double.parse("3.14") // 3.14
b := Bool.parse("true")   // true

Process.doc:
A running program, from `process.spawn`.
  `pid`   — its process id
  `args`  — what was run
  `code`  — exit code once it has finished (after `wait`, `done` or
            `communicate`); -1 before

ProcessError.doc:
Thrown by `run(check=true)`, `shell(check=true)` and `output` when the
program exits with a non-zero code. The message names the command, the
exit code and the first line of its stderr.

ProgressBar.doc:
How far along something is: `value` out of `max` (clamped), drawn as a
filled bar. `show_text` adds the percentage. Set `value` as work
progresses.

Pty.doc:
A program running in a pseudo-terminal (from `pty.spawn`). `exit_code`
is set once it has ended (-N: killed by signal N).

PtyError.doc: Thrown when a program can't be started in a pseudo-terminal.

Queue.doc:
A double-ended queue (deque) supporting O(1) push/pop at both ends.
Useful for BFS, sliding windows, and task scheduling.

@example:
q := Queue()
q.push_back(1)
q.push_back(2)
q.push_front(0)
print(q.pop_front())  // 0
print(q.peek_front()) // 1
print(q.size())       // 2

RadioGroup.doc:
One choice out of `options` (anything with `.str()`), shown as a column
of round buttons. Click one, or Up / Down (Left / Right) when it has the
focus. `selected` is the index (-1 = none); `on_change(index, item)` runs
when it changes.

Regex.doc: A compiled regular expression. Construct via `regex.compile(pattern, flags)`.

Request.doc:
A parsed incoming HTTP request — what `Server` hands to your handler.

  `method`   — uppercase verb (`GET`, `POST`, …).
  `path`     — request path with query stripped (e.g. `/users/42`).
  `query`    — Map of query-string params (parsed via `url.parse_query`).
  `headers`  — Map of header name → value (case-preserved as received).
  `body`     — request body for POST/PUT, "" otherwise.

An incoming request, as a handler sees it:
  `method`  — "GET", "POST", ... (upper case)
  `path`    — "/users/42" (decoded, without the query)
  `url`     — the request target as sent ("/users/42?tab=1")
  `query`   — Map of the query string ("?tab=1" → {"tab": "1"})
  `params`  — Map of the route's `:name` / `*name` parts
  `headers` — Map of headers, names in lower case
  `body`    — the raw body (bytes kept as they came)
  `locals`  — a Map for middleware to pass things to handlers
`json()`, `form()`, `cookies()`, `header(name)` read the rest.

Response.doc:
HTTP response.
  `status_code`  — numeric status (200, 404, ...).
  `headers`      — Map of header name → value (header names are
                   case-preserved as the server returned them).
  `text`         — decoded response body (chunked encoding handled).
  `ok`           — true iff `200 <= status_code < 300`.

The answer a handler builds: `res.status(201).json(value)`,
`res.html(page)`, `res.redirect("/login")`, `res.file("report.pdf")`,
`res.set("X-Name", "v")`, `res.cookie("session", id)`. The first send
wins; it's written when the handler (and middleware) return.

Result.signature: type Result[T, E] = Ok(value: T) | Err(error: E)

Router.doc:
The app's live pages, in one place (a `router.qk`, say):

    from live use { Router }
    from src.counter use { CounterPage }
    from src.todos use { TodoPage }

    router := Router()
    router.add("/", CounterPage)
    router.add("/todos", TodoPage)
    router.add("/users/:id", UserPage)       // self.param("id") in the page

and in the app, `app.mount("/", router)`. It's a `web.Router`, so it can
hold ordinary routes too (`router.get("/api/items", handler)`). Mount it
at "/" (the browser script talks to /_live/).

A group of routes and middleware to mount in an app under a prefix:

    api := web.Router()
    api.get("/users", list_users)
    app.mount("/api", api)          // GET /api/users

Row.doc: Widgets side by side, `spacing` pixels apart (wrapping when the window is narrow).

Children side by side, each as tall as the row. Free width goes to
children with `expand = true`.

RunResult.doc:
A finished program.
  `args`       — what was run
  `code`       — exit code; `-N` when it was killed by signal N
  `stdout`     — everything it wrote to stdout ("" when not captured)
  `stderr`     — everything it wrote to stderr ("" when not captured or
                 merged into stdout)
  `timed_out`  — killed because `timeout_ms` passed
  `ok`         — `code == 0`

ScrollView.doc:
Shows `content` (any widget, usually a Column) in an area `height`
pixels tall that scrolls when the content is taller: mouse wheel, drag
the scroll bar, or Tab to a widget that's out of view. `offset` is how
far it's scrolled (pixels). With `expand` it takes its container's free
height instead.

Server.doc:
A simple HTTP/1.1 server. Each connection is handled in its own task, so
requests are served concurrently: while one handler waits (on a socket,
`sys.sleep`, or `await`), others run.

Session.doc:
A visitor's session: values kept on the server between their requests.
The browser only holds a random id, signed, in an HttpOnly cookie. Get it
with `req.session()` (after `app.use(web.sessions())`).

SessionStore.doc:
Where sessions are kept: `web.memory_store()` (the default — the server's
memory: they end when it restarts) or `web.sqlite_store(...)` (a SQLite
database: they last across restarts and deploys). A store of your own is a
struct with these methods.

Slider.doc: A number picked with a handle; `on_change(value)` when it's moved.

Pick a number between `min` and `max` by dragging (or with the arrow
keys, by `step`). `on_change(value)` runs when it moves.

Socket.doc:
TCP socket. Wraps an OS file descriptor and provides high-level
`bind`/`listen`/`accept`/`connect`/`send`/`recv`/`close` operations.
All failure modes raise `SocketError`.

Spacer.doc: Empty space that pushes the widgets after it in a Row to the end.
Empty space that takes whatever its container has left over.

SplitView.doc:
Two widgets side by side (or stacked: `vertical=true`) with a divider
you drag to share the space. `ratio` is the first pane's share in
percent; `min_size` the smallest a pane gets (pixels). It takes its
container's free space (`expand`) unless told otherwise.

SqliteStore.doc:
Sessions in a SQLite database (tables `quirk_sessions` and
`quirk_session_meta`, made if they aren't there — it can be your app's own
database: `db.migrate` isn't affected). Their values are kept as JSON:
Strings, numbers, Bools, null, Lists and Maps (a struct, store its fields).

StatusBar.doc:
A strip of text sections along the bottom of a window:
`ui.StatusBar(["Ready", "Ln 1, Col 1"])`. The first section takes the
free space; the others are right-aligned. `set(i, text)` changes one.

String.signature: struct String : Primitive, Comparable, Sizeable, Iterable, Representable {
String.doc:
An immutable UTF-8 string. String literals use double or single quotes.
Supports interpolation with `"Hello ${name}"`, iteration over characters,
and a rich set of transformation and query methods.

@example:
s := "Hello, world!"
print(s.upper())            // "HELLO, WORLD!"
print(s.contains("world")) // true
parts := s.split(", ")
print(parts.length())       // 2

StringResult.doc:
Parsed string result paired with the index of the closing quote so
the caller can detect trailing junk.

Table.doc:
A table: `columns` the header texts, `rows` a List of rows (each a List of
cells — text or widgets). With `on_select`, a row can be clicked:
`on_select(index, row)`.

Rows of values under column headers: `ui.Table(["Name", "Size"], rows)`,
each row a List (anything with `.str()`). Columns size to their content
(or set `widths`); click a row (or Up / Down) to select it, click a
header to sort by that column (again: reverse). `on_select(index, row)`
runs when the selection changes — `index` into `rows`, whatever the sort.
With `editable=true` a cell can be changed in place: Left / Right pick
the column, Enter / F2 or a double-click edit it, Enter saves, Escape
cancels. The new value goes into `rows` (an Int column stays an Int when
the text is a number) and `on_edit(index, column, value)` runs.

Tabs.doc:
Pages under a row of tabs: `ui.Tabs(["General", "Advanced"], [page1, page2])`.
Click a tab, or Left / Right when the tab row has the focus. `selected`
is the page shown; `on_change(index, title)` runs when it changes;
`add(title, page)` adds one, `close(i)` removes one.
`closable=true` puts a × on each tab: clicking it (or middle-clicking the
tab) calls `on_close(index)` — say, to ask about unsaved changes, then
`close(index)` — or, without an `on_close`, closes the tab.

TestCase.doc:
A single named test. Construct with `TestCase("name", fn() { ... })`.
The lambda body uses `test.assert_*` helpers; any AssertionError fails
the case. Other exceptions also fail it (their type is shown).

TestClient.doc:
Call an app's routes without a network, for tests:

    client := web.TestClient(app)
    res := client.get("/users/1")
    test.assert_eq(res.status_code, 200)
    test.assert_eq(res.body, "...")

Cookies the app sets are sent back on later requests, like a browser.

TestSession.doc:
Drive live pages in tests, without a browser: s := live.TestSession(app) s.open("/") s.send("inc") test.assert_true(s.html.contains("

1

")) `html` is the component's current HTML; `title` its title.

TextArea.doc: A text field of several lines; `on_change(text)` as the user types.

Multi-line text. Enter starts a new line; Up / Down / Page Up / Page Down
move between lines, Home / End to the start / end of the line (with Ctrl:
of the text). Editing, selection and copy / paste as for `TextEdit`.
`rows` / `columns` set the size it asks for; it scrolls (wheel, or by
following the cursor) when the text is bigger. With `wrap=true` long
lines break at spaces to fit the width (and the keys move along the
wrapped lines) instead of scrolling sideways. `on_change(text)` runs on
every edit.

TextEdit.doc:
What TextInput and TextArea share: the text, a cursor and a selection,
and the editing keys.
  `text`             — the contents; set it to replace them
  `cursor`           — position (0 = before the first character)
  `has_selection()`, `selection_start()`, `selection_end()`,
  `selected_text()`, `select(start, end)`, `select_all()`
  `insert(s)`        — type `s` at the cursor (replacing the selection)
  `copy()`, `cut()`, `paste()` — through the system clipboard
  `undo()`, `redo()` — Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z
Keys: Shift + arrows / Home / End select, Ctrl+A selects everything,
Ctrl+C / X / V copy, cut and paste (Cmd on macOS), Ctrl + Left / Right
move by word, Ctrl + Backspace / Delete erase a word. Mouse: click to
place the cursor, drag or Shift+click to select, double-click selects a
word, triple-click a line.

TextInput.doc:
A one-line text field. `on_change(text)` runs as the user types (after a
short pause), `on_submit(text)` on Enter. Show the page's state in it
(`text=self.draft`); set that to "" in on_submit to clear the field.

A one-line text field. Type when it has the focus (click it or Tab to
it); editing, selection and copy / paste as described for `TextEdit`.
`on_change(text)` runs on every edit, `on_submit(text)` on Enter.
`columns` sets its width in characters.

Theme.doc:
Colours and sizes every widget draws with. Make your own by changing a
copy of `ui.dark()` / `ui.light()`.
  `background` — the window; `surface` — panels; `text`, `muted` — text

then: a folder read lazily).

under the mouse, the selected row tinted (outlined while focused), thin
chevrons, and a click on a parent opens / closes it. `row_height`,
